findings.disposition_note: The run is closed as negative evidence with product and tests restored to base, this review is read-only, and the figure is retained as the record of that measurement; redrawing it would not change the measured claim, and the caption names each seed set and its perturbation scale.
findings.evidence: attached image-0.png: grey polyline running through all six category positions with markers at x 195..1301.5; report.py:195-205 calls ax.plot(range(6), counts[arm][1], ...) for both arms with no marker-only branch.
findings.summary: The six seed sets are nominal categories plotted as a continuous line, so the render joins 'common' and 'perturbation 1' to 'perturbation 5' with straight segments and the grey series draws a hump (7 at perturbation 2, 15 at perturbation 3, 9 at perturbation 4) that exists only because an order was assigned to labels. The seed sets are independent random perturbations of the initial moments at 1e-14 relative, with no ordering, so the connecting segments imply an interpolation and a trend the data do not have, and a reader can take the 15 at perturbation 3 as a dose-response rather than one independent sample. The figure's actual claim is unaffected, because the flat blue line at 20 against the grey spread of 7 to 15 reads the same without the segments, and each category is individually labelled.

findings.disposition_note: The caption directly above the figure supplies the normalisation, the comparative claim is unaffected, and the run is closed negative evidence that this read-only review cannot redraw.
findings.evidence: attached image-0.png y axis title at x about 85, and the plotted values 20 against 8,8,7,15,9,8 read from the marker centres; the fragment caption and the run manifest both describe a shared sixteen-lane batch read.
findings.summary: The y axis title reads 'Fresh batch reads' without saying that each read is one full-batch evaluation shared by all sixteen lanes, so a reader can take the head value of 20 as a per-lane count or as a count of individual read calls, when it is the number of whole-batch evaluations the slowest lane forced every lane to pay. The run's evidence fragment states 'Sixteen lanes share every batch read' in the caption, so the page carries the normalisation, but the axis that carries the numbers does not, and the figure read on its own (a slide, a screenshot) loses the distinction that makes the 20-against-7..15 comparison mean anything.

rubric_lines: RUBRIC legibility: pass. One 14 x 7.2 in panel of a two-series line chart: six nominal seed sets across the x axis ('common', 'perturbation 1' to 'perturbation 5'), fresh batch reads on a 0-20 y scale. The blue series is a flat line at 20 across all six, the grey series runs 8, 8, 7, 15, 9, 8. Axis titles, tick labels and both legend entries are readable at the delivered size.

RUBRIC data_ink: pass. The canvas carries two polylines, twelve round markers, five y ticks with labels, six x tick labels, two axis titles and a two-entry legend. No gridlines, no baseline band, no fills, no annotations.

RUBRIC decoration: pass. White ground throughout, no gradient, no background fill, no shaded band, no drop shadow, no theme styling; only the left and bottom spines are drawn and the top and right are absent.

RUBRIC contrast: pass. Axis and tick text is #52514e (82,81,78) at 7.94:1 on white; the base grey #929292 measures 3.11:1, at the 3:1 floor this style sets for a non-text data mark; the head blue #3366cc measures 5.37:1. No text or mark is lost to lightness.

RUBRIC table_form: pass. Six seed sets against two arms is a small number of values, but the figure's job is the shape the table cannot show: the blue series is constant at 20 while the grey series varies 7 to 15. That flat-against-varying contrast is a plotted relationship rather than a lookup, and the run's evidence fragment carries the full numeric table beside the figure.

RUBRIC label_collision: pass. No text touches a canvas edge: dark text pixels span x 74..1369 of 1399 and y 18..659 of 720, with zero dark pixels in the outer 4 px frame on any side.
